Harden shim startup-failure record path resolution against a TOCTOU race between Path::canonicalize() and cap_std::fs::Dir::open_ambient_dir() in no_follow_diagnostics_dir (src/shim/mod.rs). An attacker with same-user filesystem race capability could replace the workspace root or an ancestor directory between the two calls. Closing this fully would require capability-based directory handles threaded through from a trusted root rather than re-resolving from a path string, a larger architectural change beyond 124-F scope, and this exact canonicalize-then-open pattern is already used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. canonicalize_workspace itself). Harden shim startup-failure record write against a hard-link attack (src/shim/mod.rs write_startup_failure_record): FollowSymlinks::No plus a regular-file check still accept a pre-created hard link at the leaf path, allowing a process with workspace write access to redirect the append onto a same-filesystem file the operator owns. Validate the opened handle's link count/identity via platform-specific metadata (refuse nlink > 1), or redesign storage to avoid reusing an attacker-provided leaf name entirely (e.g. a fresh per-process/per-timestamp filename). Advisory from 124-F (870B1AFF) Copilot review on PR #349; requires pre-existing workspace write access (same privilege level as many other trusted-workspace-content assumptions already made by the shim/daemon), accepted as a follow-up rather than a 124-F blocker.
